result.summary: The image shows a residential street with paved sidewalks on both sides, separated from the roadway by grass buffers. The street is wide and lacks lane markings or traffic calming measures, which may lead to higher vehicle speeds. Mature trees and residential landscaping provide shade but also create some visual obstructions for pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from vegetation
hazards.description: Large trees and bushes near the sidewalk and roadway edge can obscure sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the street

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to physically slow vehicle speeds on this residential block.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add center line and parking lane markings to narrow the perceived travel lanes and organize traffic.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim trees and bushes to maintain clear sightlines at potential crossing points and along the sidewalk.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a very narrow sidewalk separated from the roadway by a small grass buffer. There is a lack of pedestrian-specific infrastructure such as marked crossings, street lighting, or ADA-compliant walkways, which limits the safety and accessibility of the environment.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk is significantly narrower than standard, which may force pedestrians into the roadway or make it difficult for those with mobility aids to pass.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the far side of the street between the grass and the curb.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street lamps are visible on the utility poles, creating potential safety issues for pedestrians after dark due to poor visibility.
hazards.location_in_image: Utility poles along the street edge.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the existing walkway to at least 5-6 feet to meet ADA standards and improve pedestrian comfort.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install luminaires to improve visibility and security for people walking at night.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: If this is a common crossing point, add marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space.

result.summary: This residential street lacks dedicated pedestrian infrastructure, with no sidewalks or marked crossings visible. Pedestrians are forced to walk in the roadway or on unpaved grassy areas, while parked vehicles on the left create sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: The absence of paved walkways forces pedestrians into the travel lane, significantly increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left curb block the view between pedestrians and drivers, making crossings more dangerous.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the left side of the street where cars are parked.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a dedicated and safe space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with appropriate signage to designate safe crossing locations and alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.
